$comment: Ouro UI for Windows and for Android, as their READMEs and X-ray sources say at the commits below (site/src/platforms/). platforms.test.tsx holds each component list to scripts/parity-data/platforms.json.

apple.name: Ouro UI for Apple
readmeSays: SwiftUI components for people and App Intents for agents.
Both, from one declaration | a command line, MCP and WebMCP tools and a web control | an App Intent, a SwiftUI button and a Reins action
Every component keeps 44-point targets, crossfades under Reduce Motion, has VoiceOver names, wraps at the largest text sizes
It also has VoiceOver read every page of the gallery's macOS build

windows.name: Ouro UI for Windows
windows.feedLine: dotnet nuget add source https://nuget.pkg.github.com/ourostack/index.json --name ourostack --username <your GitHub login> --password <token> --store-password-in-clear-text
readmeSays: Each follows light and dark mode, a Windows contrast theme, the text size and the animation setting.
the agent doors (Windows App Actions and an MCP server for the On-device Agent Registry), all generated from ouro-ui-core's one defineAction declaration.
OuroComposedSurface, which draws an agent's card, as a composed tree or as A2UI messages
every button is one of your declared actions, with its label, consent class and confirm sheet taken from the catalog, never from the agent.
builds, packages and installs the MSIX, then reads the window through UI Automation in light, dark, a contrast theme, with animations off and with text at 225%.
nvda: starts NVDA through Guidepup on windows-latest, opens Ouro Shop's tables page
draws Ouro Shop's composed card and presses it as a person would
It is Windows Server: no App Actions runtime, no On-device Agent Registry and no Mica. CI proves the package registers both doors and that they behave; it can't prove Windows lists them to agents.
GitHub's NuGet feed needs a sign-in even for public packages: a token with read:packages
The .nupkg files are also attached to each release, for a local feed with no sign-in.
a yes from the person before a consequential action an agent prepared
gives each file it attaches a GitHub build attestation, so you can check that a package was built from its tag
from core's specs (`vendor/core/components`) and tokens.
Switch: a Button with the Toggle pattern, as WinUI's ToggleSwitch is. Its thumb stretches while pressed, never with Windows animations off.
Select: a WinUI ComboBox, so its list opens as a flyout and its options are 44 epx tall.
Under a contrast theme the controls draw the person's system colours, not the theme's (as Windows asks). Status tones then look alike, so their meaning must also be in words.
that opens a menu of every action, so a swipe is never the only way
that opens a menu of moves, so a drag is never the only way
Every move is announced with its place, and focus stays on the moved row's handle.
It checks every claim core makes for each component (`tools/claims.mts`)
samples pixels against what each control reports it drew
every tone and variant reads at 4.5:1 or better in all 6 themes, light and dark.
and measures launch time, memory and press latency.

The runtime every door goes through: input checked against the schema, idempotency keys, an audit of every call, a yes from the person before a consequential action an agent prepared, and core's typed refusal for a person-only action at every agent door.
The MCP server is three lines (`samples/OuroShop/OuroShop.Mcp/Program.cs`). An App Action launch is `OuroAppActionUri.Read(catalog, uri)` passed to the same runtime.
The MSIX registers its App Actions and its MCP server.
runs the X-ray (`tools/xray.mts`) that agents and people see the same actions, answers the MCP server's confirmation dialog
A Windows 11 client check (build 26220.7262 or later) would add the system App Actions catalog, `odr.exe mcp list`, an agent calling through the registry, and Mica in the screenshots.
Person-only actions: UI Automation can press their buttons. Requiring Windows Hello first is built and off
xraySays: does what agents can call agree with what people press? It reads the window's UI Automation tree,
the live MCP server's answers, the App Actions the installed package registered
doorsOf, so the X-ray and the generator can't disagree about what a door carries.
MCP call asks the person first (No is the default)
a retry with the same key runs once

android.name: Ouro UI for Android
readmeSays: core's components in Jetpack Compose for people, and AppFunctions for agents, both from ouro-ui-core's one defineAction declaration.
The claims are names and roles in the semantics tree, 48 dp touch targets, reduced motion, text that reflows at 200%, and contrast in all six themes with pixels sampled.
emulator: the sample on an Android 17 emulator, Google's automated-test image (ATD). The X-ray compares what Android indexed against the declarations.
Everything in this repository is checked on Android emulators in GitHub's CI, never on a real device.
OuroComposedSurface draws an agent's card, as Ouro's composed tree or as A2UI messages
A consequential action (one that reaches other people, such as sharing a list) never runs from an agent's AppFunction call until the person says yes.
TalkBack's own speech for Table is proven in CI's talkback job
AppFunctions need compileSdk 37 and AGP 9.1 or later.
OuroTheme from core's tokens (six themes, light and dark, increased contrast, reduce motion)
the kit stays free of Material
gives each file it attaches a GitHub build attestation, so you can check that a library was built from its tag

the overlays `OuroDialog`, `OuroSheet` and `OuroConfirmDialog` (platform windows drawn from the theme, not Material's `AlertDialog` or `ModalBottomSheet`, so the kit stays free of Material; each has a pane title, a heading and the dismiss action)
component specs are vendored from core by hash, and only the rendering is written here.
It also checks the snapshots in light, dark, increased contrast and 200% text.

A person's press and an agent's AppFunction call take one path. A person-only action refuses agents with core's typed refusal, and a consequential one asks the person first with a built-in confirmation (`OuroConfirm`), which an app can replace with its own `confirm`.
action declarations become `OuroActions.kt` (an AppFunction per action an agent may call, none for person-only) and `doors.json` (which door carries which action, and why not).
Android has no system prompt to ask for an app, so `ouro-actions` asks itself
**App on screen:** the confirmation opens at once.
a high-priority notification titled with the question. Tapping it opens the confirmation. The notification has no Allow and shows none of the values
nothing can ask, so the call is refused with `OuroNeedsPerson`
the call suspends until the person answers or two minutes pass
the timeout all mean no, and no runs nothing.
whose message says why and how to fix it.
Don't is the default button.
On CI's API 36 emulator image Android indexed none of the sample's AppFunctions, so CI checks them on Android 17 (API 37).
share runs only after the person confirms in the card's own sheet, and place order hands off without ordering
xraySays: what agents can call (the AppFunctions Android indexed for this app) and what people
can press (the buttons on screen) both come from shopping.actions.mts, and they agree with it.
